subject: Question: 24-hour Notification Exception & Evidence Handoff for EU Customer
participants_external: alice.jones@finsecure.com (Alice Jones, Head of Security, FinSecure)
body_text:
From: Alice Jones <alice.jones@finsecure.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: dpo@finsecure.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 17:12:00 +0000
Subject: Clarify evidence handoff timeline & 24h notify exception

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are reviewing the DPA language ahead of contracting and have a couple of clarification asks from our security and legal teams. Two items are blocking us:

1) The DPA currently references a 24-hour notification obligation for "material unauthorized access". For regulated bank customers in the EU we need to understand how Redwood would treat partial evidence access requests (e.g., a narrowed forensic snapshot vs full repository export) and whether you reserve any right to delay evidence transfers where a subprocessor containment is ongoing.

2) The clause describing forensic evidence handoff says "as reasonably available" and "subject to legal restraints". Our legal team is pushing for an explicit timeline for transmission of a first forensic snapshot (they propose 48 hours) and an explicit point-of-contact escalation path if Redwood cannot meet the window due to third-party subprocessors.

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood will commit to an initial snapshot within 48 hours for EU-regulated customers as a DPA addendum?
- If Redwood relies on subprocessors to produce any of the artifacts, will Redwood still accept contractual responsibility for the combined delivery timeline (i.e., you coordinate with subs and surface exceptions to us)?

If useful we can propose redline language.

Regards,
Alice Jones
Head of Security, FinSecure

----

On Mon, 15 Jan 2028 at 18:05, markus.klein@redwood.ai wrote:
From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: Alice Jones <alice.jones@finsecure.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify evidence handoff timeline & 24h notify exception

Alice —

Appreciate the specificity. Short answers up front: we can commit to a structured escalation and to taking ownership of coordination with subprocessors, but the 24-hour notify / 48-hour snapshot commitment needs careful carve-outs to be operationally safe.

High level proposal:
- Notification: Redwood will provide an initial notification to the customer within 24 hours of identifying a confirmed material incident affecting customer data. The notification will include a summary of scope, impacted workloads, and an estimated ETA for the first forensic snapshot.
- Snapshot: Redwood will provide a first forensic snapshot (metadata, relevant logs, and a minimal memory/kv snapshot sufficient for preliminary triage) within 72 hours as standard for EU-regulated customers. We can escalate to a 48-hour target for Enterprise customers on Dedicated or Private deployments via contract addendum.
- Subprocessor coordination: Redwood accepts contractual responsibility for delivery timelines. When artifacts require a subprocessor’s cooperation (e.g., cloud provider snapshots, third-party logging pipelines), we will coordinate and will: 1) notify the customer of the dependency within the initial 24-hour notice and 2) provide an escalation path with named contacts and expected timelines.

I’m copying Kim (Legal) and Grace (Security Ops) to confirm operational feasibility and to draft suggested DPA redlines.

— Mark
Markus Klein
Head of Sales (EMEA), Redwood Inference

----

On Tue, 16 Jan 2028 at 09:30, kimberly_park@redwood.ai wrote:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, Alice Jones <alice.jones@finsecure.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Jan 2028 09:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify evidence handoff timeline & 24h notify exception

Alice —

Thanks — a couple of legal points and proposed redlines below. We want to preserve clarity for auditors while keeping operational flexibility. In the DPA addendum we propose language like: 

"Notification and Evidence Handoff:
- Initial Notification: Redwood will notify the Customer without undue delay and, in any event, within 24 hours of confirming a material unauthorized access incident that impacts Customer Data.
- Forensic Snapshot: Subject to applicable law and without prejudice to Redwood's obligations to coordinate with subprocessors, Redwood will (i) produce and transfer to the Customer a preliminary forensic snapshot within 72 hours where Redwood operates Hosted or Dedicated services; (ii) where the Customer is on a Reserved or Private deployment and such service level is selected in the Order Form, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide a preliminary forensic snapshot within 48 hours.
- Subprocessor Dependencies: Redwood shall remain responsible for performing the coordination necessary to obtain artifacts from subprocessors and will clearly state any subprocessor-related delays in the initial notice. Any statutory limitations (e.g., non-disclosure under foreign law) will be identified and Redwood will provide the Customer with -- to the extent permitted -- a summary of the reason for delay and expected remediation timeline.

We also propose including a short appendix listing named contacts and an escalation ladder (Tier 1: Security Ops, Tier 2: Legal, Tier 3: Executive) and a requirement that Redwood provide weekly status updates until the final handoff is complete.

Attachments: redwood-dpa-v3.2.pdf (proposed redline), forensic_export_template.xlsx (evidence schema).

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

----

On Wed, 17 Jan 2028 at 14:05, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai wrote:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai, alice.jones@finsecure.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, dpo@finsecure.com
Date: Wed, 17 Jan 2028 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify evidence handoff timeline & 24h notify exception

Alice / Marco —

Operational confirmation from Security Ops: the 72-hour preliminary snapshot is our baseline for Hosted. For Dedicated/Private we can meet a 48-hour preliminary snapshot so long as: 
- The customer's environment is on a supported version with prefix/KV caching enabled (we need a quick pre-contract ops checklist), and
- There are no foreign government legal restraints preventing disclosure of specific subsystems (we will identify these as quickly as possible).

Our practical approach: within 24 hours we will provide a notice that includes: an incident summary, artifacts we will deliver with approximate sizes, any subprocessor dependencies, and the named Redwood contacts for each escalation tier. If a subprocessor (e.g., managed logging vendor) is the critical path, we provide a snapshot of the artifacts we already control (logs, telemetry, call traces) and a separate coordinated ETA for the subprocessor-generated artifacts.

We’re happy to include the proposed appendix (contacts + escalation ladder) in the DPA addendum and to provide the pre-contract ops checklist so you can confirm Dedicated/Private readiness.

Action items:
- Kimberly to circulate DPA redline (attached) with the proposed appendix.
- Ben to produce the pre-contract ops checklist and a short note on what telemetry artifacts we include in the 72h snapshot.
- Alice/Marco to confirm whether FinSecure will accept a 72h baseline for Hosted with a 48h committed target on Dedicated/Private.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Security Operations, Redwood Inference
